supersedes: v1 sealed 2026-11-01 6413751, before any code — the significance test was described as a p-value from a normal/t tail; refined here, still before any kernel is committed, to a sealed critical value the organ carries, so the gate is pure arithmetic a clean machine re-checks with no transcendental internals.
question: Does the growth experiment gate promote a technique to a skill ONLY when it beats the organ's sealed baseline on the sealed metric, by at least the sealed margin, at or above the sealed sample size, and its standardized effect reaches the sealed critical value in the sealed direction — judged from the data alone, never from who proposed it — and is every dropped technique kept on the record with its data?
why: Simon's growth-organs spec (2026-11-01). §2 HOW AN ORGAN LEARNS: baseline → hypothesis → sealed test (metric, sample size, comparison method, minimum improvement, written before running) → run → VERDICT by the Analyst (not the proposing organ) → PROMOTE (a versioned skill) or DROP (kept on record). §6 G1: every playbook entry links a passed experiment with its data. A technique becomes a skill only after it proves itself on OUR own numbers; outside advice is a hypothesis to test, never a rule. This kernel is that gate — pure, total, deterministic, witness-gated with zero survivors and nothing baselined.

design.where: A kernel in this public repo, src/experiment.mjs, carrying no channel secrets and no account data. A sealed test and its measured result are plain numbers the organ collected from Simon's own analytics; nothing here fetches, posts or stores a credential.
design.sealedTest: A technique's test, written BEFORE it runs: { id, channel, technique, metric, kind: 'rate'|'mean', baseline (the organ's current measured level), direction: 'higher'|'lower', minImprovement (the smallest lift worth a skill, an absolute delta on the metric), minSample (per arm, integer >= 2), alpha (the significance level the organ chose, for the record), zCrit (the critical value of the standardized effect for that alpha, method and sample — the organ seals this, e.g. 1.645 one-sided 0.05, 1.96 two-sided 0.05, 2.326 one-sided 0.01, or the t critical value it looked up for small df) }. normalizeTest refuses a test missing or malforming any field, with a reason.
design.result: What the run measured, tied to a sealed test by id: for a rate, { testId, control: {n, hits}, variant: {n, hits}, proposer? }; for a mean, { testId, control: {values:[…]}, variant: {values:[…]}, proposer? }. proposer is recorded but MUST NOT change the verdict.
design.statistic: The standardized effect in the sealed direction. rate: two-proportion z, stat = improvement / sqrt(pPooled(1-pPooled)(1/nC+1/nV)). mean: Welch, stat = improvement / sqrt(sC^2/nC + sV^2/nV) with sample variances (n-1). improvement is the directional gain (variant-control for 'higher', control-variant for 'lower'); a wrong-direction move gives a negative stat. Only sqrt and arithmetic — no p-value, no transcendental tail — so the measure re-computes it independently and no numerical internal can hide an untestable mutant. stat and improvement are rounded to 6 dp; a case clear of the critical-value boundary decides identically on every engine.
design.verdict: verdict(test, result) → { decision, improvement, stat, why }. INSUFFICIENT when either arm's sample < minSample (cannot conclude). Otherwise PROMOTE iff improvement >= minImprovement AND stat >= zCrit; else DROP. The function reads only (test, result); the proposer cannot move it.
design.playbook: promote(playbook, test, result) → on PROMOTE a new playbook with the technique as a versioned entry { technique, channel, metric, version, testId, data (the arms, improvement and stat), receipt }, its receipt the SHA-256 of the canonical (test, measurement, verdict); on anything else the skills are unchanged and the failure is appended to playbook.log with its verdict and data. No playbook entry without a passed experiment and its numbers (G1).
design.hardRules: The kernel decides promotion only; it never posts, never fetches, never judges engagement as real or fake (the auditor's and Simon's job) and carries no earnings or crypto wording. It is the measurement, not the mouth.

claims.claim: A test must be whole and a result must match it: of 120 malformed sealed tests (each missing or malforming one field) all are refused with a reason; of 120 results whose testId names no sealed test, or whose arms are malformed, all are refused; 60 whole test+result pairs are all accepted.
claims.pass: 120 of 120 refused, 120 of 120 refused, 60 of 60 accepted

claims.claim: The sample gate holds: for every case whose stat reaches zCrit and lift >= margin but either arm's sample < minSample, the decision is INSUFFICIENT, never PROMOTE.
The margin gate holds: for every well-sampled case whose stat reaches zCrit but whose lift is below the sealed minImprovement, the decision is DROP, never PROMOTE.

The significance gate holds (the anti-guru core): for every well-sampled case whose lift >= margin but whose standardized stat does NOT reach the sealed zCrit, the decision is DROP, never PROMOTE — a big-looking lift that is not statistically convincing is not a skill.
Direction holds: a move against the sealed direction (negative stat) is DROP however large.

PROMOTE only when all three hold: over the 400-case battery, every PROMOTE satisfies sample>=minSample AND lift>=minImprovement AND stat>=zCrit, each re-computed INDEPENDENTLY from the raw arms in the measure; and every case that satisfies all three is PROMOTE.
claims.pass: the kernel's PROMOTE set equals the independent all-three set, both ways

claims.claim: Playbook provenance (G1): promote() adds a versioned entry ONLY on PROMOTE, carrying the test id, the data and a receipt SHA; across the battery the skill entries equal the PROMOTE verdicts, every entry's receipt re-derives from its (test,result,verdict), and every non-PROMOTE is on playbook.log; no entry lacks a passed experiment.
claims.pass: entries == PROMOTEs; all receipts re-derive; all non-PROMOTEs logged

claims.claim: Total and deterministic: 3,000 fuzzed inputs (wrong types, missing and extra fields, NaN/Infinity/huge counts, hits>n, negative n) raise nothing — each is refused with a reason or yields a verdict that reads back; and the same input gives the same verdict and the same receipt id every time.
claims.pass: 0 throws; all handled; byte-identical on repeat

claims.claim: The Analyst judges from the data, not the proposer: for every case, changing only the result.proposer field (to each persona, to 'simon', to absent) leaves decision, improvement, stat and receipt identical.
claims.pass: verdict and receipt unchanged across every proposer

corpus.generator: tools/growth1-corpus.mjs, seed 20261101 — a battery of sealed tests and measured results spanning the decision surface: clear wins, significant-but-below-margin, above-margin-but-not-significant, wrong-direction, under-sampled and ties; rate and mean kinds. Every emitted case is kept only when it is clear of the critical-value and margin boundaries, so its decision is identical on every engine.

notProven: This seals the GATE's logic, not that any particular technique helps our real audience (each channel organ's own sealed test on live analytics, run later). The kernel APPLIES the critical value the sealed test carries; choosing a zCrit appropriate to the metric, method and sample size (one- vs two-sided, a t value for small df) is the organ's sealed responsibility, written before the run. Nothing here is about posting, platform rules or engagement authenticity (the auditor and Simon own those).
